reader.requirement: At --std 85 an OPEN I-O of a sequential file that supports READ and REWRITE must succeed and leave the file open for both input and output, and an OPEN I-O of a file that will not support the I-O-mode operations must be unsuccessful with I-O status 37 (§1985:VII.1.3.5 d.2).

edition-consulted.switches: SharingFacilityInEffect (DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility): Table 19 arbitration and buffer release; ClosedWithLock (CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector); LinageViolatingOpenLeavesFileOpen for OUTPUT only. None of them touches the I-O support question.
the default sharing mode (ALL OTHER at 85, no Table 19)
only the catch for a host sharing refusal ('30' at 85, '61' from 2002); the GR17 checks (SupportsReadOperations, PermitsWrite) are edition-independent

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectBehavior/SharingFacilityInEffect over Runtime/IO FileConnector.cs and FileRegistry.cs on the OPEN path
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the GR17 status decisions are the same code at every edition; only the sharing facility around them differs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f19_01 covers the successful OPEN I-O with READ and REWRITE; the refusal half (a file that will not support I-O) is not exercised

probes.printed: IO SA 00 / READ2 BBBB 00 / REWRITE 00 / R1 AAAA R2 ZZZZ / USE ENTERED IO PRINT 37 / IO OPTIONAL ABSENT 05 / OP AT END 10 / USE ENTERED IO ABSENT 35 / IO VA 00 VA READ 00 04 3 / VA REWRITE 00 / VA AFTER XQX
probes.expected: I-O open 00 with READ and REWRITE working (GR17); a print file (WRITE ADVANCING) will not support input: 37 (VII.1.3.5 d.2); optional absent created 05 then AT END; non-optional absent 35 (Table 1); RECORD VARYING/ODO record read and rewritten in I-O mode

probes.printed: USE ENTERED / IO READONLY 37 / INPUT READONLY 00 / READ AAAA 00
probes.expected: a read-only host file will not support output operations: OPEN I-O 37, OPEN INPUT 00

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR17  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR17
OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.3d.2

reader.notes: The I-O support question is asked once above the organizations in FileConnector.OpenOnceEntered: SupportsReadOperations (false for a record sequential print file) and HostFile.PermitsWrite on a present file, both returning '37'. Probes show the success half (READ/REWRITE in I-O mode, including a variable-length ODO record) and both refusal causes. 1985 defines no LINE SEQUENTIAL, so the print-file arm reached at 85 is the ADVANCING/LINAGE file.

refuter.evidence: q1a.cob (runs/q1a-001): OPEN I-O 00; a second OPEN I-O 41; READ 00, REWRITE 00, REWRITE again without READ 43, REWRITE of a changed record (alnum + S9(4) COMP) 00, WRITE in I-O mode 48 (Table 2: WRITE not permitted in I-O), READ to end 10 via USE; read back INPUT shows the rewritten record in place (2XYZ -0193). q1b.cob: OPEN I-O FA WITH NO REWIND refused (COBOL1803; the 1985 format admits NO REWIND only on INPUT/OUTPUT; its message cites §2023, a wording point). q1c.cob: a file whose only WRITE ADVANCING is never executed, written plainly, then OPEN I-O: 37, READ 47. That is the implementor's print-file classification (SequentialConnector.IsRecordSequentialPrintFile), documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-146.md (c') with an 85 case pb5815_print_file_not_read_back_85; under §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16 every sequential WRITE gets implicit AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE so the standard draws no print-file line itself, but GR17 makes 'supports' a property of the file the implementor's medium decides, and 37 is the status §1985:VII.1.3.5 assigns. Not decisive against the verdict. Citations: OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR17 (the text is in GR17); OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR4 (the text is in GR4); OK §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16 (the text is in GR16).
